questions.question: A product card uses border-radius, but its inner image still pokes past the rounded corners. Which declaration clips it to the curve?
questions.explanation: Setting overflow: hidden on the rounded container clips any child content that would extend past the border-radius curve.

questions.question: A theme recolors an entire site by changing one `--brand` declaration on :root that every component reads via var(--brand). What CSS feature is `--brand`?
questions.explanation: Two-dash names like --brand declare custom properties (CSS variables), which var() resolves wherever they are referenced, enabling single-point theme changes.

questions.question: A base stylesheet must pull in `theme.css` so the browser fetches it as part of the same stylesheet chain. Which at-rule does this?
questions.explanation: @import url(...) placed at the top of a stylesheet instructs the browser to fetch and apply another CSS file's rules.

questions.question: Inside `display: flex`, item A has flex-grow: 2 and item B flex-grow: 1. With 300px of free space to distribute, how much extra width does item A get?
questions.explanation: Free space splits by grow-factor ratio 2:1, so item A receives 2/3 x 300px = 200px while item B gets 100px.

questions.question: Two flex items of equal flex-basis overflow their container by 200px; item A has flex-shrink: 3 and item B flex-shrink: 1. How much does item A shrink?
questions.explanation: With equal bases, shrink amounts are proportional to the shrink factors (3:1), so item A loses 3/4 x 200px = 150px.

questions.question: A grid container declares named regions like "nav main" and "sidebar footer", and children opt into them via grid-area. Which container property defines those named regions?
questions.explanation: grid-template-areas maps quoted row strings of area names onto the grid; grid-area on children then places them into those regions.

questions.question: A developer inserts a decorative open-quote ahead of every testimonial purely in CSS: `blockquote::___ { content: "\201C"; }`. Which pseudo-element fills the blank?
questions.explanation: ::before generates a box as the element's first child, so the content declaration renders the quote ahead of the testimonial text.

questions.question: A clearfix appends an invisible block that pushes past floats: `.group::___ { content: ""; display: table; clear: both; }`. Which pseudo-element fills the blank?
questions.explanation: ::after generates a box as the element's last child; clearing it forces the container to enclose its floated children.

questions.question: A badge must pulse through opacity stops at 0%, 50%, and 100% under `animation: pulse 2s infinite`. Which at-rule defines those stops?
questions.explanation: @keyframes pulse { 0%/50%/100% } defines the intermediate style stops that the animation property plays back.

questions.question: A hero must layer a texture PNG over a photo JPEG in one declaration. Rather than the `background` shorthand, which longhand property takes the comma-separated image list?
questions.explanation: background-image is the longhand that lists one or more image sources, front layer first; the background shorthand can carry them too.

questions.question: An editorial layout must enlarge only the first character of each paragraph into a drop cap via `p::___ { font-size: 3em; float: left; }`. Which pseudo-element fills the blank?
questions.explanation: ::first-letter selects the first letter of a block container so only that glyph receives the drop-cap styling.

questions.question: A stylesheet sets `#nav { color: red }` and `.nav { color: blue }`, and both apply to one element. Which kind of selector wins the conflict?
questions.explanation: ID selectors (specificity 1-0-0) outrank class selectors (0-1-0), so the element renders red regardless of source order.

questions.question: Unlike visibility: hidden, what does display: none do to layout?
questions.explanation: display: none removes the element's space entirely.

questions.question: A stylesheet declares `.a { color: red }` before `.b { color: blue }`, and both apply to one element. Which rule's color wins, and why?
questions.explanation: Both classes share specificity 0-1-0, so source order decides: the later declaration (.b, blue) wins.

questions.question: A sidebar column is declared `width: calc(25% - 10px)` inside a 1,000px-wide container. What is its computed width?
questions.explanation: calc() resolves 25% of 1,000px to 250px, then subtracts 10px, yielding 240px.

questions.question: A designer writes `.card { container-type: inline-size; }` and `@container (min-width: 400px) { ... }` so the card restyles itself from its parent's width rather than the viewport. What CSS feature is being used?
questions.explanation: Container queries let components respond to their containing element's size instead of the viewport.

questions.question: A site header must stay pinned to the top of the viewport only while its parent section is on screen, then scroll away naturally. Which position value achieves this?
questions.explanation: position: sticky acts relative until a scroll threshold, then fixes within its nearest scrolling ancestor.

questions.question: In `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))`, which function constrains each track to a 200px minimum while letting it grow?
questions.explanation: minmax(min, max) bounds a track's size between a floor and a ceiling value.

questions.question: A developer writes `form:has(input:invalid) { border-color: red }` to style a parent based on its children. What is :has() formally classified as?
questions.explanation: :has() is the relational pseudo-class, matching an element relative to anchor elements inside it.

questions.question: A developer wants to recolor only the bullet of each <li> without touching the list text. Which pseudo-element targets list markers?
questions.explanation: ::marker selects the marker box of list items, allowing independent styling of bullets or numbers.
